problems.problem: The declared concept is 'hard-edge concentric RECTANGULAR step rings expanding from the exact centre like fresnel lens steps', but the render shows soft, blurred CIRCULAR halo bands plus a rounded-rectangle card inset with a drop-shadowed border at the canvas edges. The step geometry reads as an accidental radial glow and a framed card, not as crisp printed stair rings; against references 3-5 (each with one decisive graphic device) this background looks like a generic violet gradient with a vignette frame.

The single thin gold seam is rendered as a CIRCLE arcing out from behind the bottle's lower-right flank and re-entering under the base (visible in the contact detail crop as a gold curve crossing beneath the glass). Inside a rectangular step system a circular seam is a genre mismatch, and because it is partly occluded it reads as a stray halo ring around the product rather than as a step seam; it also crowds the base contact zone.

Hierarchy in the lower plaque band is unresolved: the 'PRADA' logotype (28px, dark ink, centered at x=421) sits left of the band center while the gold rule (decoration at x=356 width 367, center ~540) is centered, so the two plaque elements disagree on axis; the left-aligned 110px 'Paradoxe' then starts at x=162, leaving a large dead zone on the right of the band. The band reads as three unrelated placements instead of one composed plaque, unlike the confident lockups in references 3 and 5.

The renderer already rejected the light logo ink (#f4eef8 -> #261E16) for contrast below 3 on this orchid field; the surviving dark-brown logo now reads as a forced correction rather than a chosen ink, and its small size plus wide tracking makes it the weakest element of the plaque against the dominant title.

The concept's 'dimensional paradox' (flat printed stair vs. volumetric glass refraction) is undercut: the steps are soft and circular, the seam is circular, and the card frame adds a third unrelated device, so the flat-graphic side of the paradox never clearly asserts itself; the bottle's baked-in softbox speculars then float on an ambiguous field instead of playing against crisp printed geometry.

changes.value: Seamless flat matte screen-printed card in medium orchid violet, perfectly even shadowless frontal illumination, six crisp hard-edge concentric rectangular step rings in lighter lilac expanding from the exact centre of the frame like fresnel lens steps with clean 90-degree corners, one thin straight-edged rectangular gold seam line aligned to the third step, no circles, no rounded card border, no frame, no vignette, no texture gradients, no objects
